postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:36: `i.content` is nil on standard RSS 2.0 feeds (which use `<description>`), causing NoMethodError and crashing the entire poll; with retry: false the feed import never works for RSS feeds

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:36: `String#scrub` requires Ruby 2.1 but this 2013-era codebase targets Ruby 1.9/2.0 where scrub does not exist, so NoMethodError kills the job even when content is present

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. `scrub` is a `String` method that was added in Ruby 2.1; it does not exist in Ruby 1.9.x or 2.0. This diff itself suggests the codebase still considers Ruby 1.9 compatibility (e.g., Gemfile comment: "perftools only works on 1.9 atm"), so on those runtimes this line will raise `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for String` and break feed polling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:50: `open(url)` used without `require 'open-uri'`; if open-uri isn't already loaded, Kernel#open treats the URI as a filename and raises NoMethodError/ArgumentError, making TopicEmbed.import_remote fail intermittently depending on load order

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` but `app/models/topic_embed.rb` does not `require 'open-uri'`. Without `open-uri`, `Kernel#open` will not handle HTTP(S) URLs (it will try to open a local file like `"http://..."` and typically raise `Errno::ENOENT`). Although `open-uri` is required in `Jobs::PollFeed`, `import_remote` is also invoked from `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` and `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, which do not require `open-uri`, so whether it works can indeed depend on whether some other code has already loaded `open-uri` in the current process.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed_spec.rb:2: spec uses fabricated/unrelated require `require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'` instead of requiring the actual job under test (PollFeed), potentially causing LoadError or masking the intended require

adjudication.rationale: In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb the spec declares `describe Jobs::PollFeed` and instantiates `Jobs::PollFeed.new`, but it only does `require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'`, which is unrelated to the job under test. Since the implementation is added at app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, Rails/ActiveSupport autoloading would typically expect `jobs/poll_feed` for `Jobs::PollFeed`, so without explicitly requiring `jobs/scheduled/poll_feed` this spec can raise `uninitialized constant Jobs::PollFeed` (or depend on incidental preloading), making the require both incorrect and potentially test-breaking.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb:13: synchronous execution of Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) inside the backgrounded retrieve_topic job runs full feed parse plus article fetch inline; the 60-second throttle (retrieved_recently? / 1-minute cache) means the user's reload after the 30-second JS timer likely still hits the throttle path and shows the loading page indefinitely, so first-time embeds frequently never render

adjudication.rationale: The diff does include a synchronous `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` call, but it is in `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, which is invoked from the background job `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (not from `embed_controller.rb:13`). The “indefinitely never render” claim due to the 60-second throttle is not verifiable from the code: on the first request, `retrieved_recently?` will allow `perform_retrieve` to run (it sets the key and returns false), so retrieval starts; subsequent reloads may enqueue throttled jobs for up to 60s, but once the first retrieval finishes and creates a `TopicEmbed`, the controller will render the embed on the next reload regardless of the throttle. Thus the core failure mode described (frequent permanent loading due to throttle/30s reload) is a misreading/exaggeration rather than a clear defect introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embedded HTML imported via TopicEmbed.import is rendered with no sanitization: RSS feed content and Disqus readability content bypass the cook pipeline (cook_method: raw_html) and are rendered with raw post.cooked, allowing script/link injection (e.g., javascript: URLs in href/src)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `cook_method: :raw_html` path for posts imported via `TopicEmbed.import`/`import_remote`. In `Post#cook`, `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` bypasses the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. Imported content comes from `SimpleRSS.parse(open(...))` (feed) and `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` (remote HTML), then is stored as `raw` and later rendered in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. The only transformation is `absolutize_urls`, which rewrites leading `/` URLs but does not sanitize or restrict dangerous schemes like `javascript:` in `href`/`src`, nor strip `<script>` if present. Therefore untrusted imported HTML can be executed in the Discourse origin, a real XSS injection risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No error state for retrieval failure: loading view reloads every 30 seconds forever if TopicRetriever fails (host mismatch, missing user, no content found), causing an infinite reload loop

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `EmbedController#best`, when no existing `TopicEmbed` is found it always enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` and renders `embed/loading`. The loading view unconditionally reloads the page every 30 seconds (`document.location.reload()`), with no max retries and no error rendering.

If retrieval never results in a `TopicEmbed`, the user will be stuck in an infinite reload loop. The diff contains multiple verifiable paths where this can happen:
- `TopicRetriever#retrieve` skips `perform_retrieve` when `invalid_host?` is true; `EmbedController` does not validate that `params[:embed_url]` host matches `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (it only checks `request.referer` host), so a mismatched `embed_url` can lead to permanent non-retrieval.
- `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` returns silently when the embedding user can’t be found (`return if user.blank?`), so the embed is never created.
- `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` can also raise if `SiteSetting.embed_by_username` is nil (`.downcase`), causing the job to fail and still leaving no embed.
In all these cases, the controller will keep serving the loading page and the client will reload forever.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed job has no error handling per feed item or fetch: nil content/title or a failed open() raises and with retry: false a single malformed item permanently kills the hourly poll

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no rescue; `open(...)` or parsing can raise and will crash the job run. It then assumes `i.content` is non-nil (`i.content.scrub`), so a feed item missing `content` (or other unexpected types) can raise `NoMethodError` and abort the whole polling run, preventing subsequent items from importing. Also `sidekiq_options retry: false` means Sidekiq won’t automatically retry that failed run (though the scheduled job would run again on the next hourly recurrence), so transient/malformed data can cause dropped polling cycles.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import failure case unhandled for blank title/user: PostCreator returns an invalid unsaved Post so post.present? is true, TopicEmbed.create! references nil post.id violating DB constraint, raising uncaught inside the transaction
Embed view does not handle topic_id_for_embed returning deleted or restricted/private category topics; TopicView may raise or expose private-category posts to anonymous embed viewers

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, the code takes a topic_id from TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed and instantiates TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5}) without additional checks. However, whether this can “expose private-category posts to anonymous embed viewers” (or whether TopicView will raise for deleted/restricted topics) depends on TopicView/Guardian permission and error-handling behavior, which is not shown in this diff. The diff itself does not demonstrate that TopicView bypasses access control or that an exception would be unhandled in a problematic way; thus the finding is not directly verifiable from the changes presented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Iframe height only communicated on window.onload; late-loading images/avatars from other hosts leave iframe with stale/short height with no dynamic re-resize

adjudication.rationale: In the new embed layout (`app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`), the iframe height is sent to the parent only once, in a `window.onload` handler. However, `window.onload` fires after the document and its dependent resources (including `` tags like avatars in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` and images inside `post.cooked`) have finished loading. The diff does not introduce any lazy-loading or post-load DOM mutations that would change height after `onload`, so the claim about “late-loading images leaving stale/short height” is not a verifiable defect from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key (feed-modified:<sha1> cache key) is defined but never used, so conditional GET/ETag skip-polling was dropped and every feed is fully re-fetched and re-processed hourly

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the method `feed_key` is indeed defined but never referenced anywhere in the diff, so it is dead/unused code. However, the finding’s larger claim that “conditional GET/ETag skip-polling was dropped” is not verifiable from this diff: this job is newly added and there is no shown prior implementation using ETag/Last-Modified, nor any code that would have used `feed_key` to avoid re-fetching. The diff only shows that it always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` when enabled.

adjudication.rationale: The diff to `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` only removes trailing whitespace after `disable_ddl_transaction!` and changes the final newline (`\ No newline at end of file`). adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of the --category CLI option from the disqus task causes a hard crash for existing users running disqus import --category X

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` line was removed, along with all handling of `options[:category]`. Thor will reject unknown CLI options; therefore `disqus import --category X` (or `-c`) will now raise an “unknown option” error and exit non-zero instead of running, which is a breaking behavior change introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing category_id logic and the PostCreator call means imported topics no longer respect category or contain the [Permalink] body content

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the `:category` option and the associated `category_id` lookup logic were removed, and the `PostCreator.new(... category: category_id, raw: "[[Permalink](#{t[:link]})]" ...)` call was replaced with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote/import` does not accept or set a category, and the created post raw content is the fetched Readability content (plus an "Imported from" footer), not the prior explicit `[Permalink]` body. So the diff does remove category support and changes/removes the permalink-only body content for Disqus imports.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The skip_validations option added to PostRevisor is a general validation bypass not restricted to embed imports, allowing any caller to silently bypass post validations

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new capability in `PostRevisor#update_post`: `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, and the new embed import code calls `revise!` with `skip_validations: true`. However, nothing in the diff shows this option being exposed to untrusted input or used outside the controlled embed/feed import paths. The finding argues this is a problem merely because any internal caller could pass the flag, which is more of a generalized design concern than a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve invokes Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously, repurposing a scheduled job as an on-demand library call and re-parsing the entire feed inline on every /embed/best miss

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve explicitly does `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` immediately does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates all `rss.items`, importing each. This is a synchronous, inline feed fetch/parse invoked from the on-demand retrieval path (triggered when an embed URL miss occurs), repurposing the scheduled job class as a library call and potentially re-processing the whole feed each time `perform_retrieve` runs (there’s no caching/Last-Modified check in PollFeed).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The feed_key ('feed-modified:...') is defined but never used anywhere, leaving dead code that will silently rot

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, a `feed_key` method is defined (building a Redis-style key from the feed URL), but no code in that class (or in the diff’s added/changed code) ever calls `feed_key`. This makes it effectively dead/unused code as introduced by the diff, suggesting an incomplete or leftover implementation (e.g., intended conditional GET / last-modified caching).

adjudication_records.issue_text: TOCTOU check-then-insert race on embed_url in topic_embed.rb: TopicEmbed.where then create! is not atomic, concurrent retrievals both see embed blank and unique index makes second create! raise inside Topic.transaction, leaving orphaned side-effect jobs referencing rolled back post/topic ids that retry and loop

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the code does a non-atomic check-then-create: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` followed by `TopicEmbed.create!(embed_url: url, ...)` inside a transaction. With concurrent imports of the same URL, both can observe `embed.blank?` and attempt `create!`; the unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` will cause the second `create!` to raise a constraint violation, and there is no rescue/retry logic. The additional claim about “orphaned side-effect jobs referencing rolled back post/topic ids” is not directly evidenced in this diff, but the underlying race/exception scenario is real and verifiable from the code and schema changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_retriever.rb synchronously executes the entire feed poll (Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})) for a single-URL retrieval, causing a boundary/ownership inversion that imports every feed item, creates the race, can create dozens of topics, and blocks the Sidekiq worker with no timeout on the open() calls

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline (not enqueued). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and then iterates `rss.items.each` calling `TopicEmbed.import(...)` for every feed item, which can create/update many topics/posts unrelated to the single `@embed_url` being retrieved. Because this is executed inside the `retrieve_topic` Sidekiq job path (`Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute -> TopicRetriever#retrieve`), it blocks that worker and the `open(...)` calls in both `poll_feed` and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` have no explicit timeouts in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb poison-item cascading failure with no per-item isolation and sidekiq_options retry: false: CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) raises NoMethodError when a feed item lacks content, aborting the whole each loop so all subsequent items are never imported and the feed is permanently stuck

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item’s `content` is `nil` (or the item doesn’t provide `content`), calling `.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the entire `rss.items.each` and preventing subsequent items from being imported in that run. There is no per-item rescue/isolation, and `sidekiq_options retry: false` means a failing execution won’t be retried by Sidekiq (though it may run again on the next scheduled interval).

adjudication_records.issue_text: raw_html cook path (return raw) bypasses the cooking pipeline including after_post_cook filters and sanitization, and the embed view renders it with raw post.cooked, allowing javascript:/data-URI hrefs from third-party feed content to be injected verbatim into all embedding pages

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a new `cook_method` enum and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, explicitly skipping the normal cooking pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`) and `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`, using RSS/remote HTML content (from `SimpleRSS.parse` or `Readability::Document`) that is not sanitized in this diff (RSS path only does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and `absolutize_urls` only rewrites leading `/` URLs). The embed UI renders via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`. Together, this makes it verifiable that imported HTML can be emitted verbatim without the usual sanitization/filters, allowing dangerous `href` schemes (e.g., `javascript:`/`data:`) or other unsafe HTML from feed content to be injected into the embedded page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key (SHA1 of feed_polling_url) is computed and memoized but never used — no conditional fetch or dedup cache — so polling cost grows linearly with feed size, dead code signaling an unwired throttle

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the method `feed_key` computes and memoizes a SHA1 key based on `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url`, but nothing in this diff ever calls `feed_key` (nor references `@feed_key`). The polling implementation always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` and iterates `rss.items.each` every run without using any cached “last modified”/dedup marker keyed by that value. So the observation that `feed_key` is currently dead/unwired is directly verifiable from the diff, and the job will re-process the full feed list each time (even if `TopicEmbed.import` prevents duplicates at the DB level).

adjudication_records.issue_text: cook_method discriminator is a bare int with default 1 hardcoded in the migration while the mapping is a positional Enum in Post.cook_methods; reordering or inserting a symbol silently changes meaning of existing rows with no migration or error

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `posts.cook_method` as an integer with `default: 1` (migration `AddCookMethodToPosts`) while the code interprets it via `Post.cook_methods ||= Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`. Because this Enum mapping is positional (i.e., the integer values depend on symbol order / starting index), existing rows’ meaning is tied to that ordering. If someone later reorders or inserts new cook methods in the Enum, the same stored integers would map to different meanings with no migration or runtime error. This brittleness is directly introduced by the combination of the hardcoded integer default and positional Enum mapping shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embeds table has no foreign keys or unique indexes on topic_id/post_id, permitting duplicate or cross-topic embeds and orphaned rows after Topic/Post deletion, causing EmbedController#best to construct TopicView for a nonexistent topic

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `topic_embeds` with `topic_id`/`post_id` columns and only adds a unique index on `embed_url`. It’s true there are no DB-level foreign keys, and there’s no uniqueness constraint on `topic_id`/`post_id`. However, the finding overstates the impact: duplicate embeds for the same `embed_url` are already prevented by the unique index, and allowing multiple embed URLs per topic/post is not inherently a defect. The “orphaned rows after Topic/Post deletion” and resulting `TopicView` for a nonexistent topic is a plausible risk, but it is not directly verifiable from this diff because deletion behavior/cascades (`dependent: :destroy` on Topic/Post) is not shown. So as written, it’s not a clearly verifiable problem introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: loading page reloads every 30s forever with no terminal state: if RetrieveTopic fails the embedded widget shows 'Loading Discussion...' indefinitely with no error path to the visitor and no cap on the reload loop

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no TopicEmbed exists it enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) and renders the 'loading' template. app/views/embed/loading.html.erb contains a setTimeout that unconditionally calls document.location.reload() every 30000ms, with no max retry count or alternate UI/error state. If the background retrieval never creates the embed (e.g., job fails, remote fetch errors, invalid/blocked URL), the visitor will see 'Loading Discussion...' and the iframe will reload forever.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The --category CLI option (method_option :category, aliases: '-c') in lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117 was silently deleted, breaking existing import invocations using -c and causing topics to import uncategorized

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and also deletes the associated logic that looked up `category_id` and passed `category: category_id` into `PostCreator`. The new implementation calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and neither `import_remote` nor `TopicEmbed.import` accepts or sets a category. This is a backwards-incompatible CLI change: existing invocations using `-c/--category` will fail (unknown option) and there is no longer a way to import into a specified category, meaning imports will fall back to whatever default category behavior is (commonly uncategorized).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The created_at of Disqus threads is dropped because TopicEmbed.import_remote doesn't accept a created_at, so imported topics get today's date instead of the source date

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor, the previous import path explicitly set `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` when creating the topic via `PostCreator.new(...)`. The diff replaces that with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` only passes title/content to `TopicEmbed.import`, and `TopicEmbed.import` ultimately calls `PostCreator.new` without any `created_at` option. Therefore the imported post/topic will get the current timestamp rather than the Disqus thread's original date.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 was edited to add force: true to create_table :top_topics, which drops existing table data on environments where the migration already ran

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. While `force: true` would drop and recreate the table *if this migration is executed when the table already exists*, Rails will not re-run a migration that has already been applied (it’s tracked in `schema_migrations`). So on environments “where the migration already ran”, this change will not execute and thus will not drop existing data. Any data-loss scenario would require re-running/redoing the migration or an inconsistent DB state, which is speculative and not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated churn sneaking into the PR: whitespace edit to 20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb and removed blank line in post_revisor.rb:14

adjudication.rationale: The diff does include minor non-functional edits (e.g., trailing whitespace removal in 20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb and deletion of a blank line in lib/post_revisor.rb), but this is only “unrelated churn”/style cleanup. It does not introduce a bug, security issue, correctness problem, or clear defect in behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cook in app/models/post.rb:127-131 short-circuits with 'return raw if cook_method == raw_html' before Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook), so plugins relying on after_post_cook silently stop applying to imported RSS/readability posts

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Post#cook` to immediately `return raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses the existing `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` call. Since imported RSS/readability posts are created with `cook_method: :raw_html` (see `TopicEmbed.import`), those posts will no longer run `:after_post_cook` filters, potentially breaking plugins that rely on that hook for post-processing. This behavior change is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS via raw_html cook method returning unsanitized HTML rendered with raw, since RSS feed content from PollFeed is imported with no sanitization

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `raw_html` cook method where `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and sets `raw` to feed/article HTML (`absolutize_urls(url, contents)`), and `Jobs::PollFeed` imports `i.content` from an RSS/ATOM feed with only `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` (no HTML sanitization/whitelisting). The embed view then renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, which for these posts equals unsanitized `raw`. This is a verifiable stored XSS vector if the feed content includes scripts/event handlers or other dangerous markup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: HTML injection via user-influenced embed URL interpolated into single-quoted HTML attributes in topic_embed.rb, with only a weak http(s) prefix regex check

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic_embed.rb` the code appends an HTML snippet containing the unescaped `url` into both an `` attribute and the link text: ```rb contents << "... #{url}" return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\// ``` The only validation is a prefix regex (`/^https?\:\/\//`), which still allows quotes and other characters. A URL like `http://example.com/' onmouseover='alert(1)` passes the regex and will break out of the single-quoted `href`, introducing arbitrary attributes/HTML. This is then stored as `raw` with `cook_method: :raw_html` and later rendered via `raw post.cooked` in `embed/best.html.erb`, so the injected HTML would execute. The subsequent Nokogiri `HTML.fragment` processing (`absolutize_urls`) does not sanitize this and may preserve/interpret the injected attributes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Referer-based access control on /embed/best with X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL allows trivially spoofed access to private topic content with no auth
matched_golden_ids: The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core problems: using X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL (disabling clickjacking/frame restrictions) and relying on Referer-based validation that can be trivially spoofed, enabling bypass of intended protections. It doesn’t explicitly mention the nil-referer fallback to empty string, but the underlying vulnerability (weak/bypassable referer gating combined with ALLOWALL) matches the golden issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever spec mocks perform_retrieve in both success tests, leaving the Redis throttle (setnx/expire), no_throttle bypass, embed-exists check, PollFeed invocation, and fetch_http user lookup completely untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s `TopicRetriever` specs intentionally unit-test the `retrieve` method’s control flow by stubbing `retrieved_recently?` and asserting whether `perform_retrieve` is invoked. They do not stub/mask Redis directly; they simply don’t exercise `perform_retrieve`’s internals (Redis throttle, embed existence checks, PollFeed, fetch_http). That is a test-coverage suggestion rather than a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the diff, and it’s not inherently required for the spec to be valid.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbedController specs assert only response.should_not be_success, so they pass on any unrelated 500 and never verify the intended Discourse::InvalidAccess/400 semantics, allowing the referer-host security check to regress undetected

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, the failure-path examples only assert `response.should_not be_success` (e.g., “is 404 without an embed_url”, “raises an error with a missing host”, “raises an error with no referer”) and do not assert the expected HTTP status or that `Discourse::InvalidAccess`/parameter errors are raised/handled. As written, these tests would still pass if the controller started returning an unrelated 500 or different failure mode, so they do not robustly lock in the intended referer-host security behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbedController tests stub TopicView and retrieval entirely, so best.html.erb, the layout's postMessage height script, and the @topic_view.posts.present? branches have zero rendering coverage

adjudication.rationale: The spec/spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb uses controller specs without `render_views`, and it mocks/stubs collaborators (`TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed`, `TopicRetriever.new/retrieve`, and `TopicView.new`) rather than exercising the actual templates. As a result, the new templates (app/views/embed/best.html.erb, loading.html.erb, layouts/embed.html.erb) and their branches are not actually rendered/verified by these tests. However, this is a test coverage gap, not a bug/security/correctness defect introduced in the application code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed specs stub out poll_feed itself, leaving the URL fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub), user.blank? return, and TopicEmbed.import call untested; feed_key is dead/untested code

adjudication.rationale: In the added `Jobs::PollFeed` job, the spec (`spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`) only tests `execute`’s guard conditions and explicitly stubs/expects `poll_feed`, so none of `poll_feed`’s internal behavior (user lookup/early return, `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`, URL fallback to `i.id`, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, `TopicEmbed.import` call) is exercised by these tests. Also, `feed_key` is defined in `Jobs::PollFeed` but is never referenced anywhere in the diff (including within `poll_feed`), making it verifiably dead/unused code as introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed 'Supports updating the post' test only asserts cooked content, never verifying content_sha1 update, no duplicate topics, or skipping revisions for unchanged content

adjudication.rationale: The finding critiques the completeness of the spec (it doesn’t assert content_sha1 updates, absence of duplicate topics, or no-op behavior when content is unchanged). While that’s factually true about the test, it is not a verifiable defect/bug introduced by the diff itself. The implementation in TopicEmbed.import already updates content_sha1 on change and only revises when sha1 differs, so the code behavior is not shown to be wrong—only not fully tested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls non-standard-port branch (uri.port != 80 && != 443) is never exercised, and import_remote/readability extraction has zero tests

adjudication.rationale: The `absolutize_urls` non-standard-port code path (`prefix << ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443`) is reachable whenever the embed URL includes a non-default port (e.g., `http://example.com:8080/...`), so it is not “never exercised” as a correctness issue—it's simply not covered by the added specs. Likewise, `import_remote`/Readability having no direct tests is a test-coverage concern, not a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PostRevisor change @post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]) has no test for invalid raw under skip_validations: true or default validation behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes PostRevisor#update_post from `@post.save` (always validates) to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, which preserves default behavior when `skip_validations` is nil/false and only skips validations when explicitly requested. The proposed finding is about missing test coverage for invalid input under both paths, but lack of a specific test is not, by itself, a verifiable defect introduced by the diff. Also, the diff does add coverage for the new caller behavior (TopicEmbed updating via PostRevisor with `skip_validations: true`) in `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb`, though it doesn't test invalid raw cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: raw_html cook short-circuit and cook_method assignment lack unit tests asserting Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook) is actually bypassed

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new Post#cook short-circuit for cook_method == :raw_html and assigns cook_method in PostCreator. While there is no explicit test that stubs/expects Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook) to be skipped, the added spec (spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb) asserts that for imported posts using raw_html, `post.cooked == post.raw`, which effectively exercises the short-circuit behavior. In any case, “lack unit tests asserting X” is a test-coverage suggestion, not a verifiable functional/security defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true added to already-applied migration create_top_topics.rb can silently DROP TABLE IF EXISTS top_topics, destroying aggregate data when schema is rebuilt or db:migrate:redo runs
Editing the existing top_topics migration causes schema drift: migration file no longer matches what was actually run in existing databases

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing, timestamped migration (`db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`) by changing `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. That means the migration file in the repo no longer matches what was originally executed on databases that already ran this migration, which is the “schema drift” concern described. While Rails won’t normally re-run an applied migration, changing old migrations is still a real, verifiable issue for reproducibility/auditing and can be risky if the migration is ever re-executed (the new `force: true` would drop/recreate the table).

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true on new topic_embeds table in create_topic_embeds.rb can silently drop a pre-existing table and its rows, then recreate it empty

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb the migration uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`. In Rails this will drop the `topic_embeds` table if it already exists and then recreate it, which can silently delete any existing rows in that table instead of failing loudly. Even though this is a “new” migration, the `force: true` option still introduces the verified risk described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dropping and recreating topic_embeds orphans previously imported topics, causing TopicEmbed.import to create duplicate topics for the same embed URLs

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which will DROP and recreate the `topic_embeds` table if it already exists when the migration runs (Rails’ `force: true` does that). That is a real data-loss risk: any existing `topic_embeds` rows would be wiped, leaving the already-created `topics/posts` (imported earlier) no longer linked. After that, `TopicEmbed.import` would not find an existing `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and would create a new topic/post for the same URL, producing duplicates. This scenario requires the table to already exist (e.g., from a previous run/branch/manual creation), but the destructive behavior is directly in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embeds table has no foreign key constraints or ON DELETE behavior for topic_id/post_id, leaving no cleanup path for orphaned references when topics/posts are deleted

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` creates `topic_id`/`post_id` columns without DB foreign keys or ON DELETE rules, but the finding goes further and claims there is "no cleanup path" for orphaned rows. That latter part is not verifiable from this diff alone: cleanup could be handled elsewhere (e.g., `dependent: :destroy` on Topic/Post associations, soft-deletes, or background cleanup), and Discourse/Rails apps often intentionally do not use DB-level foreign keys. So while the absence of FK constraints is observable, calling it a definite defect/no-cleanup-path is not strictly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deleted topics leave dangling topic_embeds rows, causing EmbedController#best to construct a TopicView for a nonexistent topic on every request

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` simply does `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url).pluck(:topic_id).first` (no join/existence check). In `EmbedController#best`, any non-nil `topic_id` leads to `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` without handling a missing/deleted topic. The new `topic_embeds` table has no foreign keys and the model has no `dependent: :destroy` on `belongs_to :topic`/`:post`, so deleting a `Topic` or `Post` can leave a dangling `topic_embeds` row. That would cause repeated requests to `/embed/best` for that `embed_url` to keep taking the “topic exists” branch and likely raise when `TopicView` tries to load a nonexistent topic.
